exercise1.prompt: A BankAccount whose balance is protected and reached through methods

cases.name: the balance is stored as _balance and starts at zero
prints the balance after the deposit
the account is reached through get_balance and deposit
cases.describe: a BankAccount class with get_balance and deposit inside it

hiddenCases.name: get_balance reports what is actually stored

exercise1.hint: The single underscore is a message to the next programmer: this is ours, reach it through the methods. Python still lets anyone touch it, so the convention only works if you spell it the way everyone else does.

exercise2.prompt: A Person whose age is private and set only through a method that checks it

cases.name: an age of 25 is accepted and read back
prints the age
cases.describe: the age printed after it was set

cases.name: the age is reached through get_age and set_age
cases.describe: a Person class with get_age and set_age inside it

hiddenCases.name: the age is written with two underscores, so Python mangles the name
an impossible age is refused and the old one survives
a negative age is refused too

exercise2.hint: A setter that stores whatever it is handed is only a longer way of assigning the attribute. The check inside it is the reason the attribute was made private in the first place, and a refused value must leave the old one alone.

questions.prompt: What does a single leading underscore, like _balance, do?
choices: Stops any code outside the class reading it
Signals that it is internal, without enforcing anything
Renames it when the class is created
questions.explain: It is a convention between programmers. Python will still let you read it, which is why a check file can look at it directly.

questions.prompt: What does Python do with self.__age inside class Person?
choices: Nothing special, the name is just unusual
Renames it to _Person__age so subclasses do not collide with it
questions.explain: Name mangling exists to stop a subclass accidentally overwriting a parent's private attribute, not to make the value secret.

questions.prompt: What does routing access through set_age let you do that a plain attribute does not?
choices: Reject a value that makes no sense
Change how the age is stored without changing the callers
Make the attribute impossible to read
questions.explain: A method is a place to put a rule, and it is a seam: the storage behind it can change while every caller stays as it was.

questions.prompt: set_age should accept 25 and refuse ___, because the check is what makes the private attribute worth having.
questions.explain: Any age outside 0 to 150 is the answer. A setter with no rule inside it protects nothing.
